Description: The machine is operating normally with no predicted failure.
Symptoms: Machine runs normally without alarms. Stable sensor values.
Typical_Indicators: Balanced temperatures normal torque acceptable speed low tool wear
Prevention: Inspect the machine regularly and keep maintenance records
FAQ: Q: Is maintenance required? A: Continue scheduled preventive maintenance.

Description: Heat Dissipation Failure occurs when the cooling system cannot remove enough heat from the machine.
Symptoms: Machine becomes hotter than expected. Temperature warnings may appear.
Typical_Indicators: High air temperature high process temperature abnormal thermal conditions
Root_Cause: Cooling system inefficiency blocked airflow dirty cooling fan or overheating
Recommendation_3: Check temperature sensors and replace faulty cooling parts
Prevention: Keep cooling passages clean and monitor temperatures
FAQ: Q: Why does HDF happen? A: The machine cannot dissipate heat effectively.

Description: Power Failure occurs when the required mechanical power exceeds the capability of the machine.
Symptoms: Motor struggles under load. Machine may stop unexpectedly.
Typical_Indicators: High torque combined with low rotational speed
Root_Cause: Mechanical overload electrical power limitation overloaded motor
Prevention: Avoid operating above rated power limits
FAQ: Q: How can I prevent PWF? A: Avoid excessive torque and overload.

Description: Overstrain Failure occurs when excessive mechanical stress is applied to worn components.
Symptoms: High stress vibration increased cutting resistance.
Typical_Indicators: High torque together with significant tool wear
Root_Cause: Mechanical overload caused by worn tooling or excessive force
Prevention: Replace tools before excessive wear develops
FAQ: Q: What causes OSF? A: Excessive torque together with worn tools.

Description: Tool Wear Failure occurs when the cutting tool has reached the end of its useful life.
Symptoms: Poor machining quality rough surface increased vibration.
Typical_Indicators: Very high tool wear reduced machining quality
Root_Cause: Normal wear after long operation or insufficient maintenance
Prevention: Track tool wear and replace tools before the wear limit
FAQ: Q: How do I avoid TWF? A: Replace tools before they exceed their wear limit.

Description: Random Failure represents an unexpected failure that cannot be directly explained by monitored sensor values.
Typical_Indicators: No consistent sensor pattern may be present
Root_Cause: Unexpected component failure manufacturing defect electrical issue
Recommendation_3: Run diagnostic tests before returning to service
Prevention: Schedule regular inspections to reduce unexpected failures
FAQ: Q: Can RNF be predicted? A: It is difficult because it has no consistent pattern.

Description: Machine Type L is a lightweight machine designed for lower loads.
Symptoms: Lower production load lower power demand.
Typical_Indicators: Usually lower torque and lighter workload
FAQ: Q: Is L the safest machine? A: It is generally used for lighter workloads.

Description: Machine Type M is a medium-duty machine balancing performance and durability.
FAQ: Q: When is M used? A: For medium production requirements.

Description: Machine Type H is a heavy-duty machine capable of handling high workloads.
Symptoms: High production capability with increased mechanical stress.
Typical_Indicators: Higher torque and higher operating loads
FAQ: Q: Why does H require more maintenance? A: Heavy workloads increase component stress.

Description: Cooling system maintains safe operating temperatures.
Root_Cause: Fan failure blocked filters coolant issues
FAQ: Q: What happens if cooling fails? A: Heat Dissipation Failure becomes more likely.

Description: Motor inspection ensures the drive system is operating correctly.
FAQ: Q: How often should the motor be inspected? A: During every preventive maintenance cycle.

Description: Preventive maintenance reduces unexpected failures and extends equipment life.
FAQ: Q: Why is preventive maintenance important? A: It reduces downtime and repair costs.
